guideTitle: Best 16 Inch Lawn Mowers for Small Yards (2026)
metaTitle: Best 16 Inch Lawn Mowers for Small Yards
metaDescription: Six 16 inch push mowers, cordless, corded and reel, compared on motor, battery runtime, cutting height and bag size for yards up to half an acre.
expertTake: The Greenworks 40V 16 inch brushless mower is the pick for most small yards, because a brushless motor, a 40V battery platform shared with 75 plus tools and a 3 year warranty beat the competition on long term ownership. The Litheli with two 5.0Ah batteries is the best cordless value for longer mowing sessions. The LawnMaster 16 inch reel mower is the pick if you want a silent, no-fuel machine for a short, even lawn. If your lawn is bigger than about half an acre, skip every 16 inch deck here and buy a wider mower.
introParagraphs: A compact walk-behind mower is a small machine built for small lawns, tight side yards and people who want to store it in a closet. The cutting width is narrow, which means more passes, but the machine is light, easy to steer and quick to start. That makes it a different purchase from a full-size gas mower, even though the label looks similar.

This guide explains how battery, corded and reel mowers cut differently, why battery runtime claims need careful reading, and which details matter on a narrow deck. Start with the picks above for the short list, then read the reviews below to match a mower to your lawn size, grass type and storage space.

products.name: Greenworks 40V 16 Inch Brushless Push Mower with 4.0Ah Battery
products.description:
The Greenworks is the mower to start with because it handles the basics well and plugs into a bigger system. A brushless motor means no carbon brushes to wear out, a quieter sound than a brushed motor and a longer service life. It runs on a 40V battery with a 4.0Ah pack and a charger included, and the maker quotes up to about 30 minutes of runtime and a roughly 120 minute charge.

The deck is a lightweight 16 inch design aimed at small to medium yards, and a single lever moves the cut through five positions from 1.25 to 3.375 inches. It mulches or bags to the rear, so you can leave clippings on the lawn or collect them. Compared with the Litheli, which ships two 5.0Ah batteries and quotes up to 40 minutes, the Greenworks has a shorter quoted runtime from one battery, but it also has a stronger platform story, since the same 40V battery fits more than 75 Greenworks tools.

The 3 year limited warranty covers the tool and the battery, which is longer than the 1 year battery warranty on the Litheli. Ownership is easy: rinse the underside of the deck after mowing wet grass, store the battery indoors away from extreme heat or cold, and charge it before the season starts. Anyone with a yard over about half an acre should plan for a second battery or a bigger mower.
products.bestFor: Owners of small to medium yards who want a quiet brushless cordless mower and a battery platform that powers other tools.
pros: Brushless motor means no brushes to wear and quieter running
Single lever sets five cutting heights quickly
Same 40V battery fits more than 75 Greenworks tools
Three year warranty covers both the tool and the battery
cons: Quoted runtime of about 30 minutes limits yards over a third of an acre
Only one battery is included in the base kit
Rear bag capacity is not stated in the listing

products.name: Litheli 16 Inch Brushless Cordless Mower with Two 5.0Ah Batteries

specList.label: Deck
specList.value: 16 in, 5.9 in front and 7.1 in rear wheels

products.description:
The Litheli earns the value badge because it ships with the most battery capacity of any cordless pick here. Two 5.0Ah lithium ion batteries are included, quoted at up to 40 minutes of runtime, and the maker pitches the mower at lawns up to about a quarter acre. A brushless motor keeps the sound level low and removes the need for oil changes or spark plugs.

A one lever, six position height range runs from 0.98 to 2.95 inches, and the machine offers mulching or a 13.2 gallon rear bag. Compared with the Greenworks, the Litheli cuts a little lower at the bottom of the range but tops out at 2.95 inches instead of 3.375, so very tall grass is easier on the Greenworks. The Z-fold handle collapses flat for storage under a workbench, which helps if the garage is crowded.

It includes an extra blade, a bag, a charger and two quick assembly sets, and the batteries can double as a power bank for a phone. The warranty is 3 years on the tool but only 1 year on the batteries, a notable difference from the Greenworks. Ownership is routine: sharpen or swap the blade each season, rinse the deck, and keep the batteries out of a hot car or freezing shed. Treat the quarter acre claim as a ceiling, not a promise on thick grass.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a cordless mower with two batteries in the box for longer mowing sessions on a small yard.
pros: Two 5.0Ah batteries included for longer sessions
Z-fold handle folds flat for tight storage
Spare blade comes in the box
Brushless motor needs no oil or spark plugs
cons: Battery warranty is only 1 year against 3 on the tool
Highest cut is 2.95 in, lower than the Greenworks maximum
Batteries are not part of a wider tool platform

products.name: KOMASTY 40V 16 Inch 2-in-1 Cordless Mower

specList.label: Quoted runtime
specList.value: Up to 10 minutes per the listing

specList.label: Safety
specList.value: Dual action start switch, overheat protection

products.description:
The KOMASTY is a 40V brushless mower that ships with two 4.0Ah batteries and two chargers, so both packs can be recharged at once. The motor spins to as much as 3,400 RPM, and the dual batteries work together to supply power at the same time. A mulching plug and a 10.6 gallon bag let you pick between leaving clippings and collecting them.

The runtime claim deserves attention. The listing quotes up to 10 minutes of runtime, which is far below the 30 minutes quoted for the Greenworks and 40 for the Litheli. Treat that as a signal that this is a short-session mower, suited to a very small yard or a tidy-up pass, and check the figure on the product page before buying. The dual action start requires pressing a side safety button while pulling the lever, and an overheat protection will stop the mower if you push into thick, tall grass.

Assembly is described as easy, with a video guide, and a 5 position height adjustment sets the cut. Against the corded LawnMaster MEB1216K, it gives you freedom from a cord but at a shorter run time per charge. Ownership means giving the mower a break when overheat protection kicks in, keeping the batteries charged before the first cut of the season, and cleaning the deck after wet grass.
products.bestFor: Owners of very small yards who want two batteries and two chargers and mow in short sessions.
pros: Two batteries and two chargers included in the box
Brushless motor reaches up to 3,400 RPM
Dual action start switch prevents accidental starts
Mulching plug and bag give two clipping options
cons: Quoted runtime is far shorter than the Greenworks or Litheli
Overheat protection can stop the mower in thick grass
Lesser known brand with a shorter track record

products.name: LawnMaster MEB1216K 16 Inch 12 Amp Corded Electric Mower
products.description:
A corded mower has no battery to run down, so it runs as long as you have outlet and cord. The LawnMaster MEB1216K uses a 12 amp motor at 3,500 RPM, and that continuous power makes it a steady performer in damp or moderately tall grass where a small battery mower might protest. It weighs under 33 pounds, and the push handles fold for compact storage.

The tradeoff is the cord. Lawns with trees, beds and corners mean wrapping and re-routing a cable, and you need a heavy duty outdoor extension cord of an adequate gauge for the length you use. Compared with the Greenworks, it costs less to own because there are no batteries to replace, but it asks more of you in handling. Five cutting positions run from 1.4 to 3 inches, and the 8 gallon bag is smaller than the Litheli's 13.2 gallon bag.

The 8.86 inch rear wheels help on uneven ground. Ownership is minimal: no oil, no fuel, no battery to store. Inspect the cord for nicks each season, use a GFCI protected outlet and never mow over the cord. Move the cord behind you as you work, mow away from the outlet, and the cord becomes a minor nuisance instead of a hazard.
products.bestFor: Buyers with a very small, simple yard near an outlet who want the lowest long term ownership cost.
pros: No battery to charge, replace or run down mid mow
Twelve amp motor delivers steady power in damp grass
Under 33 pounds with folding handles for storage
No fuel or battery maintenance
cons: The cord limits range and complicates lawns with obstacles
Eight gallon bag is smaller than on the Litheli
Cord needs inspection and a GFCI protected outlet

products.name: LawnMaster LMRM1602 16 Inch 5 Blade Push Reel Mower

specList.label: Power
specList.value: Your push, no fuel or battery

products.description:
A reel mower is a different machine from the others here. There is no motor: as you push, the wheels spin a cylinder of blades that sweep grass against a fixed bedknife and shear it like scissors. That scissor cut is cleaner than a rotary blade's impact cut and leaves grass tips less frayed. It is silent apart from a light whirr, burns no fuel and has nothing to charge.

The limits come with the design. The LawnMaster is set to cut from 1 to 2.5 inches in four positions, so it needs grass kept short and not allowed to run to seed or to grow tall between mows. Reels struggle with thick, wet or unusually tall grass. Compared with the Earthwise 7 blade reel, the LawnMaster has fewer blades, so its cut is a little coarser, but it also pushes more easily. Neither bags the clippings.

Ownership is simple but not zero. The blades and the bedknife must stay in contact and sharp, and the reel needs periodic adjustment and cleaning, since twigs and stones can jam it. Mow often, before the grass gets long, and leave the clippings as free mulch. If you want a quiet, no emissions way to cut a small, even lawn and do not mind a little exercise, this is a good fit.
products.bestFor: Owners of small, flat, kept-short lawns who want a silent mower with no fuel, no battery and no motor.
pros: Scissor style cut is gentler on grass blades
Completely silent apart from a light whirr
No fuel, no battery, no cord to manage
Ten inch front wheels roll easily over small bumps
cons: Struggles with tall, thick or wet grass
Cutting height tops out at 2.5 inches
No bagging, and blades need adjustment and sharpening

products.name: Earthwise 1715-16EW 16 Inch 7 Blade Push Reel Mower

specList.label: Grass types
specList.value: Suited to Bermuda, Zoysia, Centipede, St. Augustine, Seashore Paspalum

products.description:
The Earthwise is a reel mower aimed at fine, low grasses. Seven alloy steel blades and a ball bearing reel give a finer cut than a 5 blade reel, because more blades make more shearing cuts per foot of travel. The cutting height goes down to 0.5 inches and up to 2.5, and the maker names bent grass, Bermuda, Zoysia, Centipede, St. Augustine and Seashore Paspalum as suitable grasses.

That makes it a better match than the LawnMaster reel for warm season turf kept short, where a low cut is the goal. It carries steel side plates and 10 inch composite wheels, and like every reel it has no motor, no fuel and no battery. Compared with the motorized picks, it is the quietest and has the smallest ownership list, but it needs the most discipline from you.

Expect more resistance when pushing, since a 7 blade reel has more blades to turn. Mow often so you only take a small amount off each time, and reduce the cut by no more than about a third of the blade height. Keep the blades sharp and in contact with the bedknife, clean the reel after mowing and store it dry. A reel is a poor fit for rough, uneven or weedy lawns.
products.bestFor: Owners of fine, warm season turf kept low who want a quiet manual mower with a fine cut.
pros: Seven blade reel makes a finer cut than five blade models
Cuts as low as 0.5 inches for short turf
Ball bearing reel and alloy blades stay sharper longer
No fuel, battery or cord to manage
cons: Takes more effort to push than a five blade reel
Poor on tall, thick, weedy or uneven lawns
No bag, so clippings fall where they cut

buyingCriteria.explanation: Runtime quotes depend on grass height, moisture and how hard you push, so treat them as best case. The Greenworks quotes up to 30 minutes from one 4.0Ah battery, the Litheli quotes up to 40 minutes from two 5.0Ah batteries, and the KOMASTY listing quotes only up to 10 minutes. A 16 inch deck cuts a narrow strip, so a quarter acre takes many passes. Match the battery to the area you actually mow, and plan a second battery for anything bigger than about a third of an acre.

A brushless motor has no carbon brushes to wear out, runs quieter and wastes less energy as heat, which stretches runtime. The Greenworks, Litheli and KOMASTY are brushless. The corded LawnMaster MEB1216K uses a 12 amp electric motor with continuous power. For a battery mower, brushless is the baseline to look for.

The cut range decides what you can do with tall grass or low turf. The Greenworks goes up to 3.375 inches, the Litheli to 2.95, the LawnMaster MEB1216K to 3 and both reel mowers stop at 2.5. A 16 inch deck on a tall lawn will bog down. Cut no more than about a third of the grass blade at once, and mow more often when grass grows fast.

Bagging keeps lawns tidy and is useful when clippings are heavy or the lawn is going to seed. The Litheli's 13.2 gallon bag is the largest here, the KOMASTY's is 10.6 gallons and the LawnMaster MEB1216K's is 8 gallons. Mulching returns finely cut clippings to the lawn and saves emptying. Reel mowers do not bag at all.

A battery system can serve trimmers, blowers and other tools, which lowers the cost of owning more tools. The Greenworks 40V battery fits more than 75 Greenworks tools and carries a 3 year warranty on both tool and battery. The Litheli batteries carry a 1 year warranty and are not part of the Greenworks system. Look at the battery warranty, because the battery is the part that wears out.

A small mower is usually chosen for easy handling and storage. The LawnMaster MEB1216K weighs under 33 pounds with folding handles, and the Litheli has a Z-fold handle that folds flat. Folding handles let a mower stand against a wall or sit under a workbench. If your garage is crowded, storage footprint matters as much as power.

specDecoder.meaning: Battery voltage describes the pack's electrical potential. Higher voltage platforms can deliver more power, but the amp-hour figure decides how long they last.
specDecoder.watchFor: Voltage alone does not predict runtime. A 40V mower with a small battery can run shorter than a lower voltage model with a bigger pack.

specDecoder.meaning: Amp-hours measure how much charge the battery stores. More Ah means longer runtime at the same voltage.
specDecoder.watchFor: Compare 4.0Ah and 5.0Ah packs only within the same voltage, and check how many batteries come in the box.

specDecoder.meaning: A corded motor's amp rating shows how much current it can draw at full load. Twelve amps at 120 V is about 1,440 W of electrical input.
specDecoder.watchFor: Higher amps do not guarantee better cutting, because blade design and deck airflow matter too.

specDecoder.meaning: Revolutions per minute of the blade or motor. Faster blades have more tip speed, which helps cut clean.
specDecoder.watchFor: The KOMASTY quotes up to 3,400 RPM and the LawnMaster MEB1216K 3,500 RPM, but RPM is no substitute for torque under load.

specDecoder.meaning: The width of grass cut in one pass. A 16 inch deck is narrow, so it makes more passes than a 21 inch mower.
specDecoder.watchFor: A narrow deck is easier to handle but takes longer on any lawn over a small size.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power source and runtime
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared battery, corded and reel designs, and for battery mowers we compared quoted runtime and battery capacity. The Greenworks quotes up to 30 minutes and the Litheli up to 40, while the KOMASTY quotes up to 10. We treated runtime as a best case figure.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cut quality and height range
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared motor type, deck size and cutting height range, from the Earthwise at 0.5 inches to the Greenworks at 3.375 inches. We also considered cut style, scissor action versus rotary impact. These are manufacturer-stated figures.

howWeEvaluated.title: Collection and clippings
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at bag capacity and mulching options, with the Litheli at 13.2 gallons, the KOMASTY at 10.6 and the corded LawnMaster at 8, and noted that reels do not bag. Clipping handling affects how often you stop to empty.

howWeEvaluated.title: Warranty and platform
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared warranty terms and platform value. The Greenworks has a 3 year warranty on tool and battery and shares its battery with more than 75 tools, while the Litheli carries a 1 year battery warranty. A longer battery warranty counts for more than a bigger headline battery.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight and storage
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated weight, folding handles and wheel sizes. The corded LawnMaster weighs under 33 pounds, and the Litheli has a flat folding handle. Easy storage matters for a small lawn mower.

howToChoose.intro: These three power sources suit different people.

cards.label: Cordless
cards.text: A battery frees you from a cord, but runtime and battery life limit it. It is the most convenient on small to medium lawns. The Greenworks, Litheli and KOMASTY are the cordless picks.

cards.label: Corded and reel
cards.text: Corded mowers never run out of power and cost less to own, but you manage a cable. Reels are silent and need no power, but they need short, even grass. The LawnMaster MEB1216K is corded, and the LawnMaster LMRM1602 and the Earthwise 1715-16EW are reels.

howToChoose.note: Pick cordless for flexibility. Pick corded for low ownership cost on a simple yard. Pick a reel for a quiet, short lawn.

howToChoose.intro: Clipping handling is the second decision axis.

rows: Mulch or bag with a platform

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A 16 inch deck makes more passes than a wider mower, so runtime and ease of handling matter more than raw power. Folding handles and low weight help on small lots with limited storage. Check the cutting height range against your grass.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Greenworks 40V 16 Inch Mower is the best all round choice with brushless power and a warranty. The Litheli is the pick if you want two batteries in the box, and the LawnMaster LMRM1602 suits a short, flat lawn with a preference for silence.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want a platform that powers other tools, a longer battery warranty or a brushless motor. The Greenworks 40V 16 Inch Mower brings a 3 year warranty on tool and battery and a platform of more than 75 tools.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your lawn is small and flat. The LawnMaster MEB1216K corded mower and the two reel mowers cost less and have nothing to charge. Put the savings toward blade sharpening.

howToChoose.note: If your lawn is bigger than about half an acre, a 16 inch deck is the wrong tool, whatever the price.

maintenance.why: Wet clippings dry into a hard crust that blocks airflow and lowers the cut quality. A quick rinse with the battery removed prevents it.
A dull blade tears grass and leaves brown tips. Remove the battery or unplug before touching the blade.
Lithium ion packs age faster in heat and freezing cold. Store at partial charge in a dry place.
A nicked cord is a shock risk. Use a GFCI protected outlet and an outdoor rated extension cord.
The blades must lightly touch the bedknife to cut. Clear twigs and clippings, and sharpen when the cut turns ragged.

faq.q: Is a 16 inch mower big enough for my yard?
faq.a: A 16 inch deck suits small yards, roughly up to a third or half an acre depending on how patient you are. It makes more passes than a 21 inch mower, so it takes longer on a big lawn. If your lawn is larger, consider a wider deck.

faq.q: How much should I budget for a 16 inch mower?
faq.a: Reel and corded mowers sit at the low end, cordless mowers in the middle, and cordless kits with several batteries toward the upper end. Add the cost of a second battery or an extension cord if you need one. A mower on a shared battery platform can save money later.

faq.q: How long does a cordless mower battery last?
faq.a: A lithium ion battery typically lasts several seasons with care, and warranties range from 1 to 3 years in this lineup. Heat and deep discharge shorten life. Store it indoors and avoid leaving it in a hot car.

faq.q: Do runtime claims mean I can mow for that long?
faq.a: No. Runtime claims are best case. The Greenworks quotes up to 30 minutes and the Litheli up to 40, but tall, thick or wet grass shortens them. Plan on less than the claim.

faq.q: Is it safe to use a corded mower?
faq.a: Yes, with care. Use a GFCI protected outlet and an outdoor rated extension cord, keep the cord behind you and never mow over it. Inspect the cord for nicks.

faq.q: Can a reel mower handle my lawn?
faq.a: A reel mower works well on short, even, fine grass cut often. It struggles with tall, thick, wet or weedy grass. If your lawn is rough, choose a motorized mower.
